task.title: Get your first prediction from the KC1 API
task.shortdesc: Train the KC1 model, start the prediction API, and send it the metrics of one software module.

ul.li: Docker with Compose version 2. Check with docker compose version.
A copy of the project: git clone https://github.com/domail2karandeshmukh-cyber/group6-kc1-defect-prediction.git, then cd group6-kc1-defect-prediction.
Internet access for the first training run, which downloads the KC1 data set.

step.cmd: Train the model. The trainer downloads KC1, compares four candidates, and saves the selected model in artifacts/.

info.p: The last lines name the model and its threshold: Selected: Logistic balanced; threshold: 0.50.

step.cmd: Start the API in the background.
Check that the API has loaded the model.
Save the metrics of a module in a file named module.json.
Send the file to the API.

result.p: The API answers with one prediction.

These outputs are real. On 19 November 2026, the project’s trainer produced the output in step 2. FastAPI’s test client recorded the answers in steps 4 and 6 by calling the API in the same process. The Docker commands come from the project’s README, and that check didn’t include them.

ul.li: Read the KC1 prediction API reference for every field and every error.
If a request fails, see Troubleshoot the KC1 API.

p.b: Try it from the API’s own page

postreq.p: The API serves an interactive page at http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, made by Swagger UI from the API’s OpenAPI description.

ol.li: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, and select POST /predict.The API’s documentation page, with POST /predict marked
Select Try it out, and paste the contents of module.json into the request body.The request body with the module’s metrics, marked
Select Execute. The page shows the status code, 200, and the same response as step 6.The server response, with the status code and the response body marked
